intro: Welcome to the vocabulary of study and serious work! Today you'll meet the Academic Word List, a famous list of words that appear in every academic subject, learn reporting verbs that show exactly how sure a writer is (claim, imply, demonstrate), and build word families like analyse – analysis – analytical. Warm-up: which English words from your own field do you read most often?
teachingNotes: The Academic Word List (AWL) was published by Averil Coxhead (Victoria University of Wellington, New Zealand) in 2000. She counted words in an academic corpus of about 3.5 million words (arts, commerce, law and science texts), left out the 2,000 most common English words (the older General Service List), and kept word families that are frequent across many subjects. Result: 570 word families in 10 sublists ordered by frequency: sublist 1 = the 60 most frequent families, sublists 1–9 have 60 each, sublist 10 has 30. AWL words make up about 10% of the words in academic texts. A word family = a headword plus its forms (analyse, analysis, analyst, analytical, analytically). Explain sublist (sub-daftar), word family (keluarga kata), collocation (kolokasi: words that often go together, from b2-collocations) and reporting verb (kata kerja pelaporan) in plain Indonesian the first time. Be honest about limits: the AWL has no subject-specific technical words (learn those from your own field), it uses British headwords (analyse, labour), and newer lists exist (e.g. the Academic Vocabulary List, 2014): mention only if asked.

Study strategy to recommend: one sublist at a time (60 families), and for each word note its family (noun / verb / adjective / adverb), one common collocation (collect data, a key factor, have an impact on, reach a conclusion) and an own sentence about the learner's field; review, and notice the words when reading. Words taught here, in themed groups. Sublist 1 (certain): data, method, approach, analyse, assess, interpret, indicate, evident, significant, concept, theory, define, derive, establish, factor, vary. Sublist 2 (certain): achieve, affect, impact, conclude, consequent (consequently), distinct, element, obtain, perceive, relevant, seek. Don't claim a sublist number for other words (demonstrate, imply, acknowledge are AWL words in later sublists; assert, note and dispute are not AWL headwords): just say 'AWL word' or 'academic word'. Indonesian bridge: many are loanwords (data, metode, analisis, konsep, teori, faktor, elemen, relevan, signifikan), which helps, but the trap is the word class and the form. Traps: consequently = akibatnya, NOT konsekuen (Indonesian konsekuen = consistent); affect is a verb, impact (on) is the safe noun in formal writing (impact as a verb is common, especially in American English, but some readers dislike it: don't test it); effect is the noun; data has no plural -s ('datas' ✗; the data show / shows are both accepted); seek – sought – sought; establish = mendirikan (a company) or membuktikan / memastikan (establish a link, establish that).

Reporting verbs (kata kerja pelaporan) show what a source says AND how the writer of the report sees it. Proven by evidence (reporter accepts it): show, demonstrate (membuktikan, menunjukkan), establish. A position with reasons: argue (berpendapat dengan alasan; Indonesian trap: argue with someone = bertengkar, but argue that = berpendapat). Strong, maybe unsupported: claim (mengklaim: the reporter keeps a distance), assert (menegaskan: says firmly, with confidence). Careful or indirect: suggest (mengisyaratkan, mengindikasikan; its other meaning menyarankan is B2), imply (menyiratkan). Admitting: acknowledge (mengakui, often a limitation). Disagreeing: dispute, challenge (membantah, mempertanyakan) + object (dispute the figures). Neutral: note, observe (mencatat, mengamati). Academic writing usually uses the present simple (Wulan argues that …). Strength labels are a guide, not a law: accept reasonable alternatives (argue / claim / assert for an opinion; show / demonstrate / prove / establish for proof; suggest / indicate for a sign) and only mark clear mismatches (demonstrate for an unsupported opinion, claim for a proven result, acknowledge or dispute with the wrong meaning).

The node's common errors. *'The author infers that prices will rise' → implies: the writer or speaker implies (menyiratkan: puts a hidden meaning in), the reader or listener infers (menyimpulkan: takes it out), usually infer from. Some native speakers use infer for imply in casual speech, but academic writing keeps them apart. *'The study demonstrates about the effect of sleep' → demonstrates the effect (demonstrate + object or + that; Indonesian 'menunjukkan tentang', 'membahas tentang' adds about: the same error as 'discuss about'). *'This analyse shows a clear trend' → This analysis (after this / a / the you need a noun; Indonesian analisis / analisa covers several word classes, and Indonesian 'naik signifikan' leads to *'rose significant' → rose significantly).

Word families taught: analyse (British) / analyze (American) – analysis (plural analyses) – analyst (person) – analytical – analytically; significant – significance – significantly (– insignificant); interpret – interpretation – interpreter; theory – theoretical – theorise / theorize – theorist; vary – variation – variable – various (berbagai) – variety. Recap the B2 slot rule in one line (after a / the / this → noun; after be / very or before a noun → adjective; after a verb → adverb; after to / can → verb) and the B2 suffixes (-tion, -al, -ly, -ity) without re-teaching them. Stress moves: ANalyse – aNALysis – anaLYTical; THEory – theoRETical. In one text pick British or American spelling and stay consistent. Grade one thing at a time: usually the wrong family member for the slot.

Limits: a vocabulary lesson reachable straight after B2, so A0–B2 grammar only. No inversion, cleft sentences, subjunctive, impersonal passives ('It is argued that …') or advanced participle clauses in examples; 'It is evident that …' is just it + be + adjective. Don't turn this into a lesson on hedging, nominalisation or citation styles (APA, Harvard); if asked, answer briefly and come back. Keep the set manageable: don't dump whole sublists on the learner. Contexts: universities in Yogyakarta, Bandung and Malang, ministries, NGOs, startups, research reports, rupiah prices; don't invent statistics about real organisations.

keyPoints.title: The Academic Word List, sublist by sublist
keyPoints.explanation: The AWL (Averil Coxhead, 2000) has 570 word families that are common in academic texts across many subjects, in 10 sublists: sublist 1 has the most frequent ones. AWL words are about 10% of the words in academic texts. Learn one sublist at a time, and for each word note its family, a collocation and your own sentence. Careful with traps: affect is a verb, impact (on) a noun; consequently means akibatnya, not konsekuen; data has no -s.

examples.en: Price is a key factor when students in Yogyakarta choose a kos.
examples.id: Harga adalah faktor utama saat mahasiswa di Yogyakarta memilih kos.

examples.en: Long working hours can affect your health.
examples.id: Jam kerja yang panjang bisa memengaruhi kesehatanmu.

examples.en: The ministry is seeking new ways to reduce plastic waste.
examples.id: Kementerian sedang mencari cara baru untuk mengurangi sampah plastik.

id.title: Academic Word List, sublist demi sublist
id.explanation: AWL (Averil Coxhead, 2000) berisi 570 keluarga kata yang sering muncul di teks akademik dari banyak bidang ilmu, dibagi dalam 10 sublist: sublist 1 berisi yang paling sering muncul. Kata AWL sekitar 10% dari kata di teks akademik. Pelajari satu sublist setiap kali, dan untuk setiap kata catat keluarga katanya, satu kolokasi dan kalimatmu sendiri. Hati-hati jebakannya: affect adalah kata kerja, impact (on) kata benda; consequently artinya akibatnya, bukan konsekuen; data tidak pakai -s.

keyPoints.title: Precise reporting verbs
keyPoints.explanation: A reporting verb tells the reader what a source says and how sure it is. show / demonstrate = proven by evidence (+ object or that, never 'about'); argue = a position with reasons; claim / assert = said strongly, maybe without proof; suggest / imply = careful or indirect; acknowledge = admit; dispute / challenge = disagree; note / observe = neutral. The writer implies (menyiratkan); the reader infers (menyimpulkan).

examples.en: The figures demonstrate a clear link between traffic and air pollution.
examples.id: Angka-angka itu membuktikan hubungan yang jelas antara lalu lintas dan polusi udara.

examples.en: The company claims that its new drink improves memory.
examples.id: Perusahaan itu mengklaim bahwa minuman barunya meningkatkan daya ingat.

examples.en: The author acknowledges that her survey only covered big cities.
examples.id: Penulis mengakui bahwa surveinya hanya mencakup kota-kota besar.

id.title: Kata kerja pelaporan yang presisi
id.explanation: Kata kerja pelaporan memberi tahu pembaca apa yang dikatakan sumber dan seberapa yakin sumber itu. show / demonstrate = terbukti dengan bukti (+ objek atau that, tidak pernah 'about'); argue = pendapat dengan alasan; claim / assert = dinyatakan dengan kuat, mungkin tanpa bukti; suggest / imply = hati-hati atau tidak langsung; acknowledge = mengakui; dispute / challenge = tidak setuju, membantah; note / observe = netral. Penulis imply (menyiratkan); pembaca infer (menyimpulkan).

keyPoints.title: Academic word families
keyPoints.explanation: One root, different jobs: analyse (verb) – analysis (noun) – analyst (person) – analytical (adjective); significant – significance – significantly; interpret – interpretation; theory – theoretical – theorise; vary – variation – variable – various. Choose the form from the slot: after a / the / this → noun ('This analyse' ✗ → This analysis); after be / very or before a noun → adjective; after a verb → adverb (rose significantly). British analyse, theorise; American analyze, theorize.

examples.en: This analysis shows that most customers shop on their phones.
examples.id: Analisis ini menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar pelanggan berbelanja lewat ponsel.

examples.en: The number of electric motorbikes in Bali has grown significantly.
examples.id: Jumlah motor listrik di Bali sudah bertambah secara signifikan.

examples.en: The course is too theoretical: we need more practical examples.
examples.id: Kursusnya terlalu teoretis: kami butuh lebih banyak contoh praktis.

id.title: Keluarga kata akademik
id.explanation: Satu akar kata, tugas berbeda: analyse (kata kerja) – analysis (kata benda) – analyst (orangnya) – analytical (kata sifat); significant – significance – significantly; interpret – interpretation; theory – theoretical – theorise; vary – variation – variable – various. Pilih bentuknya dari posisinya: setelah a / the / this → kata benda ('This analyse' ✗ → This analysis); setelah be / very atau sebelum kata benda → kata sifat; setelah kata kerja → adverb (rose significantly). Inggris British: analyse, theorise; Amerika: analyze, theorize.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one AWL word (menilai): Next month, an outside team will ___ how well the new training programme works.
guidedPractice.hint: assess (sublist 1) = to judge how good or bad something is. It comes after will, so use the base form.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with one AWL word (akibatnya): Heavy rain closed the toll road for six hours. ___, many staff arrived late for the meeting.
guidedPractice.hint: It's the adverb from the family of consequent (sublist 2). Not 'konsekuen', which means consistent in Indonesian.

guidedPractice.prompt: In his essay, Budi gives four reasons why civil servants should work from home on Fridays. Complete with one reporting verb: Budi ___ that civil servants should work from home on Fridays.
guidedPractice.hint: He takes a position AND supports it with reasons: berpendapat.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: My ___ (interpret) of the graph is different from yours.
guidedPractice.hint: After 'my' with nothing after the gap you need a noun: interpret + -ation.

guidedPractice.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: There is a lot of ___ (vary) in rice prices between provinces.
guidedPractice.hint: After 'a lot of' you need a noun: vary → variation (perbedaan, variasi).

independentPractice.prompt: Choose two words from sublist 1 (for example data, method, approach, significant, factor) and write one sentence about your work or studies.
independentPractice.hint: One of the most important factors in my job is ... / We collect data by ...

independentPractice.prompt: Think of an article or report you read recently. Write one sentence about it with argues, claims, suggests or demonstrates.
independentPractice.hint: The writer argues that ... / The report demonstrates that ...

independentPractice.prompt: Write one sentence about something that has changed significantly in your city in the last five years.
independentPractice.hint: ... has grown / fallen / changed significantly since ...

assessment.prompt: Complete with one AWL word (dampak). Write the whole word: The new toll road has had a positive imp___ on small businesses along the route.
assessment.rubric: Correct: impact (sublist 2; a noun: have an impact on = berdampak pada). 'impacts' = 60 (after 'a' you need the singular). 'effect' = 70 (right meaning and grammar, but the task gives the first letters imp-). 'affect' = 20 (a verb: it can't follow 'a positive'). Spelling slip that keeps the word clear ('impac', 'impakt') = 70.

assessment.prompt: Complete with one AWL word (memperoleh): Researchers must ___ permission from the school before they interview any students.
assessment.rubric: Correct: obtain (sublist 2; obtain permission = memperoleh izin, a typical collocation). 'secure' is also accepted. 'get' = 60 (right meaning, but too informal for a research report). 'seek' = 60 (seek permission = meminta izin, not memperoleh). 'ask' = 30 (needs 'for'). 'obtains' / 'obtained' = 50 (after must you need the base form).

assessment.prompt: A large, careful experiment with 2,000 drivers in Jakarta measured their sleep and their reaction times. Complete with one reporting verb that tells the reader the result is proven by evidence: The experiment ___ that tired drivers react more slowly.
assessment.rubric: Correct: demonstrates / shows (or proves, establishes, confirms; present or past): a large experiment gives evidence, so the reporting verb presents the result as proven. 'demonstrate' / 'show' without -s = 80 (experiment is singular). 'suggests' / 'indicates' = 50 (too careful for a proven result). 'claims' / 'argues' / 'asserts' = 20 (they present it as an opinion; claim even signals doubt). Adding 'about' ('demonstrates about') = 50 (demonstrate takes that or an object, never about).

assessment.prompt: Pak Hasan's email to the team never mentions job cuts, but it talks about 'difficult decisions' and 'a smaller structure next year'. Complete with one verb (menyimpulkan): From the email, most of the staff ___ that some jobs would be cut.
assessment.rubric: Correct: inferred (the readers take the hidden meaning out of the email: infer from = menyimpulkan); concluded / deduced are also accepted. 'infered' = 80 (spelling: double r). 'infer' / 'infers' = 60 (right verb, but the sentence is in the past). 'understood' / 'guessed' / 'assumed' = 60 (understandable, but not the precise word for menyimpulkan). 'implied' = 0 (the email implies; the staff infer: the classic mix-up).

assessment.prompt: Dr. Wulan's paper on online learning in village schools ends with this sentence: 'Our sample of 40 schools was small.' Complete with one reporting verb (mengakui): Dr. Wulan ___ that her sample was small.
assessment.rubric: Correct: acknowledges (mengakui: she admits a weakness in her own study); admits / concedes / recognises are also accepted, present or past. 'acknowledge' without -s = 80. 'notes' / 'states' / 'says' = 60 (true, but neutral: they don't show she is admitting a weakness). 'claims' / 'argues' = 20 (they make an admission sound like a disputed opinion). 'disputes' = 0 (the opposite meaning).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: Bu Ani's report gives a careful ___ (analyse) of rice prices in Java over the last ten years.
assessment.rubric: Correct: analysis (after 'a careful' with 'of' after the gap you need a noun). 'analisis' / 'analysys' = 70 (Indonesian-style spelling or a slip: English is analysis). 'analyses' = 50 (a plural after 'a'). 'analyst' = 20 (that's the person). 'analytical' = 10 (an adjective). 'analyse' / 'analyze' = 0 (the verb: the classic 'This analyse' error).

assessment.prompt: Complete with the right form of the word in brackets: After the new bus route opened, sales at the traditional market in Bogor rose ___ (significant).
assessment.rubric: Correct: significantly (it says how sales rose: after a verb you need an adverb, adjective + -ly). 'significantely' / 'significently' = 80 (spelling). 'significant' = 20 (copies Indonesian 'naik signifikan': English needs the adverb). 'significance' = 0 (a noun).

material.title: What is the Academic Word List?

blocks.text:
When you read a journal article, a textbook or a long report, some words come up in **every subject**: *data, method, significant, analyse, factor*. In **2000**, the New Zealand researcher **Averil Coxhead** collected those words in the **Academic Word List (AWL)**.

How she made it: she counted the words in about **3.5 million words** of academic texts from arts, business, law and science. She **left out the 2,000 most common English words** (*make, house, because*: you already know them) and kept the words that are frequent in **many** subjects, not just one.

The result:
- **570 word families**. A **word family** (keluarga kata) is one word with all its forms: *analyse, analysis, analyst, analytical, analytically*.
- **10 sublists** (sub-daftar), ordered by frequency: **sublist 1** has the 60 most frequent families, sublist 2 the next 60, and so on. Sublists 1–9 have 60 families each; sublist 10 has 30.
- AWL words make up about **10%** of the words in academic texts: roughly **one word in ten**.

What it doesn't have: the technical words of one field (*photosynthesis, depreciation*). Learn those from your own textbooks.

id.text:
Saat kamu membaca artikel jurnal, buku teks atau laporan panjang, ada kata-kata yang muncul di **semua bidang ilmu**: *data, method, significant, analyse, factor*. Pada tahun **2000**, peneliti Selandia Baru **Averil Coxhead** mengumpulkan kata-kata itu dalam **Academic Word List (AWL)**.

Cara membuatnya: dia menghitung kata dalam sekitar **3,5 juta kata** teks akademik dari bidang seni dan humaniora, bisnis, hukum dan sains. Dia **membuang 2.000 kata bahasa Inggris yang paling umum** (*make, house, because*: kamu sudah tahu semuanya) dan menyimpan kata yang sering muncul di **banyak** bidang, bukan hanya satu.

Hasilnya:
- **570 keluarga kata**. **Keluarga kata** (word family) adalah satu kata beserta semua bentuknya: *analyse, analysis, analyst, analytical, analytically*.
- **10 sublist** (sub-daftar), diurutkan dari yang paling sering muncul: **sublist 1** berisi 60 keluarga kata yang paling sering, sublist 2 berisi 60 berikutnya, dan seterusnya. Sublist 1–9 masing-masing berisi 60 keluarga kata; sublist 10 berisi 30.
- Kata AWL sekitar **10%** dari kata di teks akademik: kira-kira **satu dari sepuluh kata**.

Yang tidak ada di AWL: istilah teknis satu bidang (*photosynthesis* = fotosintesis, *depreciation* = penyusutan). Itu dipelajari dari buku teks bidangmu sendiri.

blocks.text:
**How to study the AWL.** Don't try to learn 570 families at once. Take **one sublist at a time** (60 families: a few each day), and for every word write down three things:
- its **family**: *analyse* (verb), *analysis* (noun), *analytical* (adjective)
- one **collocation** (kolokasi: words that often go together, from B2): *collect data, a key factor, reach a conclusion*
- **your own sentence** about your work or studies
Then review the list every few days and notice the words when you read. **Good news for Indonesian speakers:** many AWL words are loanwords in Indonesian (*data, metode, analisis, konsep, teori, faktor, elemen, relevan, signifikan*), so the meaning is easy. The hard part is the English **form**: *analysis*, not *analisis*; *significantly*, not *significant*, after a verb.

id.text:
**Cara belajar AWL.** Jangan mencoba menghafal 570 keluarga kata sekaligus. Ambil **satu sublist setiap kali** (60 keluarga kata: beberapa setiap hari), dan untuk setiap kata catat tiga hal:
- **keluarga katanya**: *analyse* (kata kerja), *analysis* (kata benda), *analytical* (kata sifat)
- satu **kolokasi** (collocation: kata-kata yang sering muncul bersama, dari B2): *collect data* (mengumpulkan data), *a key factor* (faktor utama), *reach a conclusion* (sampai pada kesimpulan)
- **kalimatmu sendiri** tentang pekerjaan atau kuliahmu
Lalu ulangi daftarnya setiap beberapa hari dan perhatikan kata-kata itu saat membaca. **Kabar baik untuk penutur bahasa Indonesia:** banyak kata AWL sudah diserap ke bahasa Indonesia (*data, metode, analisis, konsep, teori, faktor, elemen, relevan, signifikan*), jadi artinya mudah. Bagian yang sulit adalah **bentuk** bahasa Inggrisnya: *analysis*, bukan *analisis*; *significantly*, bukan *significant*, setelah kata kerja.

blocks.prompt: Which description of the AWL is right?
options: 570 word families; sublist 1 has the most frequent ones
570 word families; sublist 10 has the most frequent ones
2,000 everyday words; sublist 1 has the easiest ones
blocks.explain: The AWL has 570 word families in 10 sublists, ordered by frequency: sublist 1 = the 60 most frequent. The 2,000 most common everyday words were left out on purpose.

id.explain: AWL berisi 570 keluarga kata dalam 10 sublist yang diurutkan dari yang paling sering muncul: sublist 1 = 60 yang paling sering. 2.000 kata sehari-hari yang paling umum justru sengaja tidak dimasukkan.

blocks.text:
Here are some of the most useful words from the first two sublists, in small groups, with a typical collocation for each.

**Sublist 1 · Doing research**
- **data** (data): *collect / analyse data*
- **method** (metode): *a research method*
- **approach** (pendekatan): *a new approach to the problem*
- **analyse** (menganalisis): *analyse the results*
- **assess** (menilai): *assess the risk*
- **interpret** (menafsirkan): *interpret the figures*

**Sublist 1 · Ideas and evidence**
- **concept** (konsep) and **theory** (teori): *a key concept, a theory of learning*
- **define** (mendefinisikan): *define a term*
- **derive from** (berasal dari, memperoleh dari): *derive income from tourism*
- **establish** (mendirikan; also memastikan, membuktikan): *establish a company, establish a link*
- **factor** (faktor): *a key factor*
- **indicate** (menunjukkan, mengindikasikan) and **evident** (jelas terlihat): *It is evident that …*
- **significant** (signifikan, cukup besar atau penting): *a significant difference*
- **vary** (bervariasi, berbeda-beda): *Prices vary from city to city.*

**Sublist 2 · Results and effects**
- **achieve** (mencapai): *achieve a goal*
- **affect** (memengaruhi, a verb) and **impact** (dampak, a noun): *have an impact on*
- **conclude** (menyimpulkan): *conclude that …*; **consequently** (akibatnya), from the family of *consequent*
- **obtain** (memperoleh): *obtain permission / data*
- **seek** (mencari, berusaha; formal): *seek advice*; past *sought*
- **perceive** (memandang, menganggap): *perceive something as a risk*
- **relevant** (relevan): *relevant to the topic*
- **distinct** (jelas berbeda, khas) and **element** (unsur): *a distinct style, a key element*

id.text:
Berikut beberapa kata paling berguna dari dua sublist pertama, dalam kelompok kecil, masing-masing dengan kolokasi yang umum.

**Sublist 1 · Melakukan penelitian**
- **data** (data): *collect / analyse data* (mengumpulkan / menganalisis data)
- **method** (metode): *a research method* (metode penelitian)
- **approach** (pendekatan): *a new approach to the problem* (pendekatan baru terhadap masalah itu)
- **analyse** (menganalisis): *analyse the results*
- **assess** (menilai): *assess the risk* (menilai risikonya)
- **interpret** (menafsirkan): *interpret the figures* (menafsirkan angka-angkanya)

**Sublist 1 · Gagasan dan bukti**
- **concept** (konsep) dan **theory** (teori): *a key concept* (konsep kunci), *a theory of learning* (teori belajar)
- **define** (mendefinisikan): *define a term* (mendefinisikan istilah)
- **derive from** (berasal dari, memperoleh dari): *derive income from tourism* (memperoleh pendapatan dari pariwisata)
- **establish** (mendirikan; juga memastikan, membuktikan): *establish a company* (mendirikan perusahaan), *establish a link* (membuktikan adanya hubungan)
- **factor** (faktor): *a key factor* (faktor utama)
- **indicate** (menunjukkan, mengindikasikan) dan **evident** (jelas terlihat): *It is evident that …* (jelas terlihat bahwa …)
- **significant** (signifikan, cukup besar atau penting): *a significant difference* (perbedaan yang signifikan)
- **vary** (bervariasi, berbeda-beda): *Prices vary from city to city.* (Harga berbeda-beda dari kota ke kota.)

**Sublist 2 · Hasil dan dampak**
- **achieve** (mencapai): *achieve a goal* (mencapai tujuan)
- **affect** (memengaruhi, kata kerja) dan **impact** (dampak, kata benda): *have an impact on* (berdampak pada)
- **conclude** (menyimpulkan): *conclude that …*; **consequently** (akibatnya), dari keluarga kata *consequent*
- **obtain** (memperoleh): *obtain permission / data* (memperoleh izin / data)
- **seek** (mencari, berusaha; formal): *seek advice* (meminta saran); bentuk lampaunya *sought*
- **perceive** (memandang, menganggap): *perceive something as a risk* (menganggap sesuatu sebagai risiko)
- **relevant** (relevan): *relevant to the topic* (relevan dengan topiknya)
- **distinct** (jelas berbeda, khas) dan **element** (unsur): *a distinct style* (gaya yang khas), *a key element* (unsur utama)

blocks.text:
**Four traps.**
- **affect** is a verb, **impact** is the safe noun: *Noise affects sleep.* / *Noise has an impact on sleep.* (*effect* is also a noun: *an effect on*.) *impact* as a verb is common, especially in American English, but some readers dislike it in formal writing.
- **consequently** = *akibatnya*. It is NOT Indonesian *konsekuen*, which means *consistent* (taat asas).
- **data** has no -s: *the data*, never *'datas'*. Both *the data show* and *the data shows* are used.
- **seek** is irregular: *seek – sought – sought*.

id.text:
**Empat jebakan.**
- **affect** adalah kata kerja, **impact** kata benda yang aman: *Noise affects sleep.* / *Noise has an impact on sleep.* (*effect* juga kata benda: *an effect on*.) *impact* sebagai kata kerja sering dipakai, terutama di bahasa Inggris Amerika, tapi sebagian pembaca tidak suka di tulisan formal.
- **consequently** = *akibatnya*. BUKAN *konsekuen* dalam bahasa Indonesia, yang artinya *consistent* (taat asas).
- **data** tidak pakai -s: *the data*, tidak pernah *'datas'*. *the data show* dan *the data shows* dua-duanya dipakai.
- **seek** tidak beraturan: *seek – sought – sought*.

blocks.prompt: Changes in the exchange rate can ___ the price of imported wheat.
blocks.explain: After can you need a verb that means memengaruhi: affect. effect is usually a noun (an effect on); its rare verb use means 'to make something happen' (effect change), which doesn't fit. effective is an adjective.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: Changes in the exchange rate can ___ the price of imported wheat.
id.explain: Setelah can kamu butuh kata kerja yang berarti memengaruhi: affect. effect biasanya kata benda (an effect on); sebagai kata kerja (jarang) artinya 'mewujudkan' (effect change), yang tidak cocok di sini. effective adalah kata sifat.

material.title: Reporting verbs: how sure is the writer?

id.title: Kata kerja pelaporan: seberapa yakin penulisnya?

blocks.text:
A **reporting verb** (kata kerja pelaporan) introduces what a source says: *Wulan **argues** that …*, *The report **shows** that …*. In B2 you used *say, tell, suggest, admit*. In academic writing the verb also tells the reader **how sure** the source is and **what you think of it**. Academic writing usually uses the present simple: *Wulan argues*.

- **show / demonstrate** (menunjukkan, membuktikan): proven by evidence; you accept it. *+ that* or *+ an object*.
- **argue** (berpendapat dengan alasan): a position, supported by reasons.
- **claim** (mengklaim): says something is true, maybe without proof; you keep your distance.
- **assert** (menegaskan): says it firmly and confidently, maybe without support.
- **suggest** (mengisyaratkan, mengindikasikan): a careful, tentative idea.
- **imply** (menyiratkan): says it indirectly, without saying it in words.
- **acknowledge** (mengakui): admits something, often a weakness or the other side.
- **dispute / challenge** (membantah, mempertanyakan): disagrees. *+ an object*: *dispute the figures*.
- **note / observe** (mencatat, mengamati): neutral; just mentions it.

id.text:
**Kata kerja pelaporan** (reporting verb) memperkenalkan apa yang dikatakan sebuah sumber: *Wulan **argues** that …*, *The report **shows** that …*. Di B2 kamu sudah memakai *say, tell, suggest, admit*. Di tulisan akademik, kata kerjanya juga memberi tahu pembaca **seberapa yakin** sumber itu dan **bagaimana pendapatmu** tentangnya. Tulisan akademik biasanya memakai present simple: *Wulan argues*.

- **show / demonstrate** (menunjukkan, membuktikan): terbukti dengan bukti; kamu menerimanya. *+ that* atau *+ objek*.
- **argue** (berpendapat dengan alasan): sebuah sikap, didukung alasan.
- **claim** (mengklaim): menyatakan sesuatu benar, mungkin tanpa bukti; kamu menjaga jarak.
- **assert** (menegaskan): menyatakannya dengan tegas dan yakin, mungkin tanpa dukungan bukti.
- **suggest** (mengisyaratkan, mengindikasikan): gagasan yang hati-hati, belum pasti.
- **imply** (menyiratkan): menyampaikannya secara tidak langsung, tanpa mengucapkannya.
- **acknowledge** (mengakui): mengakui sesuatu, sering kelemahan atau pendapat pihak lain.
- **dispute / challenge** (membantah, mempertanyakan): tidak setuju. *+ objek*: *dispute the figures* (membantah angka-angkanya).
- **note / observe** (mencatat, mengamati): netral; hanya menyebutkan.

rows.en: The figures demonstrate a clear link between traffic and air pollution.
rows.id: Angka-angka itu membuktikan hubungan yang jelas antara lalu lintas dan polusi udara.

rows.en: Dr. Wulan argues that free school meals improve attendance, and she gives three reasons.
rows.id: Dr. Wulan berpendapat bahwa makan siang gratis di sekolah meningkatkan kehadiran, dan dia memberi tiga alasan.

rows.en: The company claims that its new drink improves memory.
rows.id: Perusahaan itu mengklaim bahwa minuman barunya meningkatkan daya ingat.
rows.note: no proof: the writer keeps a distance

rows.en: The study suggests that short breaks may improve concentration.
rows.id: Penelitian itu mengisyaratkan bahwa istirahat singkat bisa meningkatkan konsentrasi.

rows.en: The author acknowledges that her survey only covered big cities.
rows.id: Penulis mengakui bahwa surveinya hanya mencakup kota-kota besar.

rows.en: Several economists dispute the minister's figures.
rows.id: Beberapa ekonom membantah angka-angka dari menteri.

blocks.text: **imply or infer?** The **writer or speaker implies** (menyiratkan): they put a meaning in without saying it. The **reader or listener infers** (menyimpulkan): they take that meaning out. *The minister's speech **implied** that taxes would rise. Journalists **inferred** from it that taxes would rise.* So *'The author infers that prices will rise'* is wrong: the author **implies** it. You met this in B2 reading as *makna tersirat*: the writer makes it *tersirat*, the reader works it out. (Some native speakers mix the two in casual speech, but academic writing keeps them apart.)

id.text: **imply atau infer?** **Penulis atau pembicara imply** (menyiratkan): mereka memasukkan makna tanpa mengatakannya. **Pembaca atau pendengar infer** (menyimpulkan): mereka menangkap makna itu. *The minister's speech **implied** that taxes would rise.* (Pidato menteri menyiratkan bahwa pajak akan naik.) *Journalists **inferred** from it that taxes would rise.* (Para wartawan menyimpulkan dari pidato itu bahwa pajak akan naik.) Jadi *'The author infers that prices will rise'* salah: penulisnya **implies**. Kamu sudah bertemu ini di pelajaran membaca B2 sebagai *makna tersirat*: penulis membuatnya tersirat, pembaca yang menangkapnya. (Sebagian penutur asli mencampur keduanya dalam percakapan santai, tapi tulisan akademik memisahkannya.)

blocks.text:
**No 'about' after demonstrate.** Indonesian says *menunjukkan tentang* or *membahas tentang*, so learners write *'The study demonstrates about the effect of sleep'*. In English, **demonstrate** takes an object or *that* directly: *The study **demonstrates the effect** of sleep.* / *… **demonstrates that** sleep matters.* (The same trap: *discuss the problem*, not *'discuss about the problem'*.)

**Two more traps.** *argue **with** someone* = bertengkar, but *argue **that** …* = berpendapat dengan alasan. And *suggest* can mean *menyarankan* (*I suggest a break*), but in a report *The data suggest that …* means *mengisyaratkan*.

id.text:
**Tidak ada 'about' setelah demonstrate.** Bahasa Indonesia bilang *menunjukkan tentang* atau *membahas tentang*, jadi pelajar menulis *'The study demonstrates about the effect of sleep'*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **demonstrate** langsung diikuti objek atau *that*: *The study **demonstrates the effect** of sleep.* / *… **demonstrates that** sleep matters.* (Jebakan yang sama: *discuss the problem*, bukan *'discuss about the problem'*.)

**Dua jebakan lagi.** *argue **with** someone* = bertengkar, tapi *argue **that** …* = berpendapat dengan alasan. Dan *suggest* bisa berarti *menyarankan* (*I suggest a break*), tapi di laporan *The data suggest that …* berarti *mengisyaratkan*.

blocks.prompt: A small survey of 30 students found that some of them study better with music. The researchers say more research is needed. The survey ___ that music may help some students study.
blocks.explain: A small survey and 'more research is needed' = a careful, tentative result: suggests. demonstrates presents it as proven, which 30 students can't do. disputes means disagrees, which makes no sense here.

id.prompt: Survei kecil terhadap 30 mahasiswa menemukan bahwa sebagian dari mereka belajar lebih baik sambil mendengarkan musik. Para peneliti bilang masih perlu penelitian lebih lanjut. Lengkapi: The survey ___ that music may help some students study.
id.explain: Survei kecil dan 'masih perlu penelitian lebih lanjut' = hasil yang hati-hati dan belum pasti: suggests. demonstrates menyajikannya sebagai sudah terbukti, padahal 30 mahasiswa tidak cukup. disputes artinya membantah, yang tidak masuk akal di sini.

options: The report demonstrates about the risks of the new dam.
The report demonstrates the risks of the new dam.
The report demonstrates on the risks of the new dam.
blocks.explain: demonstrate takes its object directly: demonstrates the risks. No about (from Indonesian 'menunjukkan tentang') and no on.

id.explain: demonstrate langsung diikuti objeknya: demonstrates the risks. Tanpa about (dari bahasa Indonesia 'menunjukkan tentang') dan tanpa on.

material.title: Word families: one root, many jobs

id.title: Keluarga kata: satu akar, banyak tugas

blocks.text:
In B1 and B2 you built words with endings like **-tion**, **-al**, **-ity** and **-ly**, and chose the form from its **slot** (posisi dalam kalimat): after *a / the / this / my* → **noun** (kata benda); after *be / very* or before a noun → **adjective** (kata sifat); after a verb → **adverb** (kata keterangan: how); after *to / can / will* → **verb** (kata kerja). Academic word families work the same way:

- **analyse** (v) → **analysis** (n; plural *analyses*) → **analyst** (n, the person) → **analytical** (adj) → *analytically* (adv)
- **significant** (adj) → **significance** (n) → **significantly** (adv); opposite *insignificant*
- **interpret** (v) → **interpretation** (n) → *interpreter* (n, the person; also a juru bahasa)
- **theory** (n) → **theoretical** (adj) → **theorise** (v) → *theorist* (n, the person)
- **vary** (v) → **variation** (n, perbedaan) → **variable** (n / adj, variabel; berubah-ubah) → **various** (adj, berbagai) → *variety* (n, *a variety of*)

**Stress moves** in some families: *ANalyse – aNALysis – anaLYTical*, *THEory – theoRETical*.

**British vs American:** *analyse, theorise* (British) / *analyze, theorize* (American). Both are correct; in one text, choose one and stay consistent.

id.text:
Di B1 dan B2 kamu membentuk kata dengan akhiran seperti **-tion**, **-al**, **-ity** dan **-ly**, dan memilih bentuknya dari **posisinya** dalam kalimat: setelah *a / the / this / my* → **kata benda** (noun); setelah *be / very* atau sebelum kata benda → **kata sifat** (adjective); setelah kata kerja → **adverb** (kata keterangan: bagaimana); setelah *to / can / will* → **kata kerja** (verb). Keluarga kata akademik bekerja dengan cara yang sama:

- **analyse** (kk) → **analysis** (kb; jamak *analyses*) → **analyst** (kb, orangnya: analis) → **analytical** (ks, analitis) → *analytically* (adv)
- **significant** (ks) → **significance** (kb, arti penting) → **significantly** (adv, secara signifikan); lawannya *insignificant*
- **interpret** (kk, menafsirkan) → **interpretation** (kb, tafsiran) → *interpreter* (kb, orangnya; juga juru bahasa)
- **theory** (kb) → **theoretical** (ks, teoretis) → **theorise** (kk, berteori) → *theorist* (kb, ahli teori)
- **vary** (kk) → **variation** (kb, perbedaan, variasi) → **variable** (kb / ks, variabel; berubah-ubah) → **various** (ks, berbagai) → *variety* (kb, *a variety of* = beragam)

(kk = kata kerja, kb = kata benda, ks = kata sifat.)

**Tekanan suku kata berpindah** di beberapa keluarga: *ANalyse – aNALysis – anaLYTical*, *THEory – theoRETical*.

**British vs Amerika:** *analyse, theorise* (British) / *analyze, theorize* (Amerika). Dua-duanya benar; dalam satu tulisan, pilih satu dan konsisten.

rows.en: This analysis shows that most customers shop on their phones.
rows.id: Analisis ini menunjukkan bahwa sebagian besar pelanggan berbelanja lewat ponsel.

rows.en: My cousin works as a data analyst for a bank in Jakarta.
rows.id: Sepupu saya bekerja sebagai analis data di sebuah bank di Jakarta.

rows.en: Nobody understood the significance of the discovery at first.
rows.id: Awalnya tidak ada yang memahami arti penting penemuan itu.

rows.en: The app is available in various languages, including Javanese.
rows.id: Aplikasi itu tersedia dalam berbagai bahasa, termasuk bahasa Jawa.
rows.note: various = berbagai, before a plural noun

id.note: various = berbagai, sebelum kata benda jamak

blocks.text:
**The Indonesian trap.** In Indonesian, *analisis* or *analisa* can be the thing (*analisis ini*) and the base of the verb (*menganalisis*), and *signifikan* works after a verb with no change (*naik signifikan*). English needs a different form for each job:
- *'This analyse shows a clear trend'* ✗ → **This analysis** shows a clear trend. (after *this* → noun)
- *'We need to analysis the data'* ✗ → We need to **analyse** the data. (after *to* → verb)
- *'Sales rose significant'* ✗ → Sales rose **significantly**. (after a verb → adverb)

id.text:
**Jebakan bahasa Indonesia.** Dalam bahasa Indonesia, *analisis* atau *analisa* bisa jadi bendanya (*analisis ini*) sekaligus dasar kata kerjanya (*menganalisis*), dan *signifikan* dipakai setelah kata kerja tanpa berubah (*naik signifikan*). Bahasa Inggris butuh bentuk berbeda untuk setiap tugas:
- *'This analyse shows a clear trend'* ✗ → **This analysis** shows a clear trend. (setelah *this* → kata benda)
- *'We need to analysis the data'* ✗ → We need to **analyse** the data. (setelah *to* → kata kerja)
- *'Sales rose significant'* ✗ → Sales rose **significantly**. (setelah kata kerja → adverb)

blocks.prompt: The difference between the two groups was very small and not statistically ___.
blocks.explain: After was (a form of be) and the adverb statistically you need an adjective: significant. significance is a noun and significantly an adverb.

id.prompt: Lengkapi: The difference between the two groups was very small and not statistically ___.
id.explain: Setelah was (bentuk be) dan adverb statistically kamu butuh kata sifat: significant. significance adalah kata benda dan significantly adverb.

id.intro: Selamat datang di kosakata untuk kuliah dan pekerjaan serius! Hari ini kamu berkenalan dengan Academic Word List, daftar terkenal berisi kata-kata yang muncul di semua bidang ilmu, belajar kata kerja pelaporan yang menunjukkan dengan tepat seberapa yakin seorang penulis (claim, imply, demonstrate), dan membangun keluarga kata seperti analyse – analysis – analytical. assessment.awv-1: Lengkapi dengan satu kata AWL (dampak). Tulis kata lengkapnya: The new toll road has had a positive imp___ on small businesses along the route.
assessment.awv-2: Lengkapi dengan satu kata AWL (memperoleh): Researchers must ___ permission from the school before they interview any students.
assessment.awv-3: Sebuah eksperimen besar dan cermat terhadap 2.000 pengemudi di Jakarta mengukur tidur dan waktu reaksi mereka. Lengkapi dengan satu kata kerja pelaporan yang memberi tahu pembaca bahwa hasilnya terbukti dengan bukti: The experiment ___ that tired drivers react more slowly.
assessment.awv-4: Email Pak Hasan untuk timnya sama sekali tidak menyebut pengurangan karyawan, tapi membahas 'difficult decisions' dan 'a smaller structure next year'. Lengkapi dengan satu kata kerja (menyimpulkan): From the email, most of the staff ___ that some jobs would be cut.
assessment.awv-5: Makalah Dr. Wulan tentang pembelajaran online di sekolah-sekolah desa diakhiri dengan kalimat ini: 'Our sample of 40 schools was small.' Lengkapi dengan satu kata kerja pelaporan (mengakui): Dr. Wulan ___ that her sample was small.
assessment.awv-6: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: Bu Ani's report gives a careful ___ (analyse) of rice prices in Java over the last ten years.
assessment.awv-7: Lengkapi dengan bentuk yang tepat dari kata dalam kurung: After the new bus route opened, sales at the traditional market in Bogor rose ___ (significant).
